title: Reproduce a crash from its record: the seed, the tick, the line, then a demo that walks it
note: When a look says the game crashed: open the record's file:line, replay its seed to its tick, fix the cause, and keep a demo that walks the crash path.
intent: A look that says "the game crashed: <kind> ... at <file:line:column> on tick N (seed S)" read the host's genex-crash/1 record (game.crashes names it). Open that file and line first: it is where the panic was raised, and the top frames are the game's own callers (the panic machinery is left out). Reproduce it before fixing: seed S, pause, then step to tick N (step runs round(ms / 16.667) ticks). When the line says the record holds input from tick A to N, the crash needed that input: write a demo that injects the same keys after the seed and advances to tick N. A crash that does not come back on that path is nondeterminism (a clock, thread_rng, HashMap or a thread), not the line it named. Fix the cause and never catch the panic: catch_unwind loses the record and leaves the state broken. Keep the demo and a probe of the end state, so every later look walks the crash path. A gpu-validation or device-lost record names the GPU error instead of a line, and a line saying the same crash ended more runs is not fixed yet.
port: The facet whose file the record names owns the fix and the demo; a crash in src/main.rs or src/game.rs is the entry owner's.

evidence.note: A panic's record names the seed, the tick it happened on and the last summary, so an agent can replay it with seed and step.
A simulation replays bit for bit from its seed on every destination: a crash that does not repeat on the same seed and input is nondeterminism.
